level_1.description: Rename SSA variables using inspection-derived symbol table
rules: Use ONLY variable names identified in the inspection results
Rename ALL SSA variables exactly once using a deterministic mapping
Do NOT introduce new variables not present in inspection metadata
Preserve use-def chains exactly as defined in inspection
Do NOT modify operations, operands, or ordering
Do NOT modify tensor types or shapes
Ensure all renamed variables still satisfy SSA dominance rules
Do NOT infer or assume missing variables
Ensure output strictly matches inspected dependency graph
Result must pass mlir-opt without modification

level_1.description: Reorder independent operations based on inspected dependency graph
rules: Use dependency graph from inspection results as the ONLY source of truth
Reorder ONLY operations marked as independent in inspection metadata
Do NOT reorder operations with direct or indirect dependencies
Do NOT move operations across blocks or regions
Maintain SSA validity and dominance constraints
Do NOT introduce or remove operations
Do NOT infer independence beyond inspection data
Ensure reordered program matches inspected data flow

level_1.description: Rename block arguments and region variables using deterministic mapping
rules: Rename ALL block arguments (e.g., ^bb0(%arg0, %arg1)) using a deterministic naming scheme
Apply renaming consistently across all uses within the region
Do NOT modify operation order or structure
Do NOT modify operands, attributes, or result types
Preserve all region and block boundaries exactly
Do NOT introduce new arguments or remove existing ones
Ensure SSA dominance and scoping rules are preserved
Do NOT rename values outside region argument scope unless explicitly required
Ensure renamed program is structurally identical except for argument names
Must produce a non-identical program text

level_1.description: Apply deterministic renaming and formatting using inspection metadata
rules: Use inspection metadata to derive naming scheme
Rename variables consistently across all occurrences

level_1.description: Normalize operation attributes and formatting without changing semantics
rules: Reformat operation attributes into canonical MLIR textual form
Normalize spacing, ordering of attributes, and delimiter usage
Convert equivalent attribute representations to a canonical form (e.g., reorder dictionary attributes)
Do NOT modify operations, operands, or result types
Do NOT modify control flow, regions, or block structure
Do NOT introduce or remove attributes
Ensure all transformations are syntax-level only
Ensure resulting MLIR is semantically identical
Must produce a non-identical textual representation

level_2.description: Modify tensor dimensions using inspection-derived shape metadata
rules: Use ONLY tensor shapes provided in inspection results
Apply modifications consistently across all dependent operations
Update all uses of modified tensors based on inspection graph
Do NOT introduce new shapes not derived from inspection
Ensure all shape transformations remain valid

level_2.description: Modify tensor element types using inspection metadata with enforced transformation
rules: Extract all unique element types from inspection metadata
Select at least one tensor element type and replace it with a different type from the extracted set
The replacement type must be different from the original type (no no-op allowed)
Apply the type change consistently across all dependent operations and values
Propagate the new type through the entire use-def chain
Update all related constants, operands, and results to match the new type
Ensure all operations used support the updated type
Do NOT introduce types not present in inspection metadata
Do NOT partially update types; all dependent uses must be updated
Maintain valid MLIR typing and SSA rules
If no alternative type exists, return explicit mutation failure instead of unchanged program
Output must be syntactically different from input

level_2.description: Modify constants based on inspection-provided values
rules: Use constants identified in inspection metadata
Modify only within valid bounds of usage
Do NOT introduce new constants outside inspection

level_2.description: Modify indexing maps using inspection-derived mappings
rules: Use ONLY indexing maps from inspection results
Apply consistent transformation across all related ops
Do NOT introduce new indexing patterns

level_2.description: Modify iteration space using inspection-provided bounds
rules: Use iteration bounds from inspection metadata
Adjust loops consistently across all dependent ops
Do NOT introduce new iteration ranges

level_3.description: Transform linalg operations using inspection-validated ops only
rules: Use ONLY operations observed in inspection results
Do NOT introduce new or unknown operations
Replace operations only with valid equivalents

level_3.description: Decompose operations based on inspection-derived structure
rules: Break operations into components derived from inspection
Ensure all intermediate values are valid

level_3.description: Fuse operations based on inspection dependency graph
rules: Fuse ONLY operations marked compatible in inspection

level_3.description: Modify operator parameters using inspection data
rules: Do NOT infer new parameter sets

level_3.description: Apply semantic transformation guided strictly by inspection graph
rules: Use inspection graph as sole reference
Use dependency graph from inspection results

level_4.description: Introduce intermediates based on inspection data flow
rules: Insert intermediates only where inspection permits

level_4.description: Reorganize blocks and regions using inspection structure
Split computation based on inspection graph
rules: Split only along valid dependency boundaries

level_4.description: Merge computation stages using inspection guidance
rules: Merge only compatible operations from inspection

level_5.description: Introduce controlled semantic failure using inspection structure
Introduce type mismatch based on inspection types
Break operator constraints using inspection-defined ops
Break dependency chain using inspection graph
Introduce structural violation using inspection metadata
